clue.text: Conceivably, bathe to make waves

blocks.note: surface reading: perhaps you could go for a swim
setter's reading: these seven letters are what you get when you shake up the last three words of the answer, so the answer is an instruction that would produce them

explanation.surface: A swimmer splashing about in the water to stir up some waves.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: rock THE BOAT (shake its letters) and you could get BATHE TO, so 'Conceivably' flags that the answer describes how the clue's words were made.
explanation.definitionFit: To make waves is an idiom for causing trouble or upsetting a settled situation, which is exactly what rocking the boat means.

clue.text: Said place is surrounded by flipping animals

indicators.note: being surrounded means having something all around you, so one piece goes inside another
to flip something is to turn it over, so these letters are read backwards

blocks.note: deer are animals
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Some location is said to be overrun by acrobatic creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' can read as a mild British curse on the animals, but it is the instruction to read them backwards; 'Said' is the definition, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reputed is commonly said or believed to be so, as in a reputed millionaire, so both mean according to report.

clue.text: Clasp found in jumble with 90 per cent off on top

indicators.text: with 90 per cent off on top
indicators.note: taking ninety per cent off a value leaves a tenth of it, so the top letter, a Roman numeral, is swapped for one worth a tenth as much

blocks.note: a jumble is a muddle

explanation.surface: A brooch turns up in a jumble sale marked down by ninety per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000; cut it by 90 per cent and 100 is left, which is C, so MUDDLE becomes CUDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold them tightly in your arms, which is a cuddle; both are verbs of affectionate holding.

clue.text: Pretty pics unusual in document

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of their ordinary order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some attractive pictures appear unexpectedly in a piece of paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty pics unusual' reads as a description of photos, but the two words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A typescript is a typed copy of a text, such as a manuscript sent to a publisher, so it is a kind of written record.

clue.text: Cash United invested in high-value deposit on the up

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so one piece is placed inside another
in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an ore is a mineral deposit worth mining
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Manchester United put money into a valuable deposit account whose value is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside ORE after its R, making ORUE, and reading that upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of most of the European Union, so it is a form of money.

clue.text: Bit of cricket – cut with energy, but too soft

blocks.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a rip is a cut or tear
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A batsman's innings: a vigorous cut shot, but played too gently.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut is also a cricket shot, which makes 'cut' look like part of the game; it is simply a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is overripe has gone past its best and become mushy, so too soft describes it well.

clue.text: Soldier, mounted, wore poor tatty clothing

indicators.note: clothing covers what is underneath, so the answer is wrapped inside these words
in a down clue, mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A cavalryman on horseback was dressed in shabby, worn-out uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' reads as on horseback, which suits a cavalry trooper, but it turns the hidden letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, especially in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Highly elated, being over-promoted

blocks.note: first meaning: overexcited, buzzing
second meaning: advertised with too much fuss

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at being raised too far up the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over-promoted' suggests a job above someone's ability; it means marketed too heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person in a state of nervous excitement and also a product given excessive publicity.

clue.text: Earth conceivably appears like a symbol of love

blocks.note: surface reading: perhaps our planet looks a certain way
setter's reading: this word is what you get if you take the organ of love and shape (rearrange) its letters

explanation.surface: Seen from space, our planet might look like a Valentine's card.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: shape HEART, rearranging its letters, and you can get EARTH, so 'conceivably' says the answer describes how that word was made.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart outline is the familiar emblem of romance, so anything with that outline looks like a love token.

clue.text: Start listing, exit listing

blocks.note: first meaning: begin to recite a list quickly
second meaning: stagger away, leaning to one side

explanation.surface: Instructions for beginning and leaving a list, like a computer menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listing' changes sense: first it is making a list, then it is leaning over like a ship, as a drunk does when he reels.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle off names is to begin reciting a series, and to lurch away unsteadily is also expressed by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Conceivably, it’s Adam or me

blocks.note: first meaning: in Genesis, Adam was the first human created
second meaning: in grammar, I and me are pronouns of this kind

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they or the biblical Adam is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conceivably' signals that each example is only one way to read the phrase; 'conceived' also hints at creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam is the earliest human in the Bible, and in grammar the speaker's own pronouns such as me belong to that category.

clue.text: Vehicle for cycling girl found in painters’ workshop?

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the first letter is moved round to the end

blocks.note: a cart is a vehicle
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A bike for a girl turns up in an artists' studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle for cycling' looks like a bicycle, but 'cycling' acts on CART, sending its C to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An art class is a session where people learn to paint, so it is a workshop for painters; the question mark marks the loose sense.

clue.text: Appropriate publicity before musical show, but no article in the end

indicators.text: but no article in the end
indicators.note: having no article at the end means the final letter, a word like 'a', is dropped

blocks.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
an opera is a musical stage show

explanation.surface: Fitting promotion before a musical, though ultimately there was nothing written about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a newspaper piece; here it is the grammatical article A at the end of OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appropriate is suitable or correct for the situation, which is what proper means as an adjective.

clue.text: Record set in athletic ground opening up closed minds?

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so these letters are broken up and reformed
a jewel set in a ring is placed inside it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
an EP, extended play, is a kind of record

explanation.surface: A world record is set in a stadium, with sporting success opening narrow minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athletic ground' looks like a stadium, but 'ground' is the anagram signal for 'athletic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is reading another person's thoughts directly, so a telepathic person could get into minds that are shut to others.

clue.text: Arrange papers to enter borders of Turkey

indicators.note: the borders of something are its edges, so only the outside letters are kept
to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Sort out documents to cross the Turkish frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' are identity documents, ID; 'borders' sounds like a frontier but takes the edge letters of the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy something is to put it in order, so as verbs both mean to organise neatly.

clue.text: Maverick takes complimentary short

blocks.note: complimentary tickets cost nothing
a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky, as opposed to a long drink

explanation.surface: A nonconformist helps themselves to a free drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective but is a British noun for a small strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent person who will not follow the crowd, which is also what an unconventional free spirit is.

clue.text: Drop Christmas on the Radio, traditional-style programme

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is identified by its sound

blocks.note: to drop something is to shed it
Yule is an old name for Christmas
the two pieces said together

explanation.surface: Scrapping the festive season from the radio schedules in favour of old-fashioned programming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traditional-style' points to the older British pronunciation 'shed-yule' rather than American 'sked-yule'.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme can be a timetable or plan of events, which is what a schedule is.

clue.text: Cheer pilot flying this?

indicators.note: things flying about are scattered and out of place, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Applaud the pilot, who is at the controls of this craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the word for what the pilot is flying is made from 'cheer pilot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot can fly a rotorcraft, so the clue taken whole points to the aircraft being flown.

clue.text: Family roll in, eager to hug

indicators.note: to hug is to hold close inside your arms, so the answer sits inside these words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Relatives arrive in a stream, keen to embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'in' is ignored when reading the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is line of descent from ancestors, so it names a family in the sense of a bloodline.

clue.text: Combo, one occasionally using this?

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A small band that now and then uses a certain woodwind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a combo, a small jazz group, might sometimes feature this instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind with a double reed is something a small band could occasionally play, so the whole sentence points to it.

clue.text: Saving or betting, as inclined?

blocks.note: first meaning: putting money in an account, or relying on something, as in counting on an outcome
second meaning: tilting sideways, as an aircraft does on turning

explanation.surface: Asking whether thrift or gambling is the way you lean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' sounds like having a preference; it is literally tilted, as a plane or a curved track is.
explanation.definitionFit: Depositing money and relying on a result share the verb, and so does an aircraft tilting its wings as it turns.

clue.text: Jasper maybe sharing million with little twins

blocks.note: jasper is a semi-precious stone
MINI means little; its M, million, is shared with the stone, so only the rest is added

explanation.surface: Someone called Jasper shares a fortune with a pair of small twin children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jasper' looks like a man's name but is the gemstone; GEM and MINI overlap on their shared M.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the constellation and star sign of the Twins, Castor and Pollux, so the Latin name means twins.

clue.text: Soundalike in speech: fool that has summer berries in it

definitions.text: that has summer berries in it

indicators.note: speech is heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a pun plays on words that sound alike
a nit is a fool; unstressed, the ending is said the same way

explanation.surface: Gooseberry fool, the pudding with summer fruit in it, is spoken of alongside wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' wants to be the dessert full of berries; it is a nitwit. A punnet is a small British basket in which soft fruit is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Strawberries and raspberries are sold in small square cardboard or plastic baskets, so the container holds summer fruit.

clue.text: Put out a call for workers in spectacles

blocks.note: to page someone is to call for them over a speaker
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Advertising for staff for an optician's glasses business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' wants to be glasses; it means grand public shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is an elaborate public show or procession, so both are nouns for impressive displays.

clue.text: Figures showing Putin’s OK, thanks

blocks.note: da is Russian for yes
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Statistics revealing that the Russian leader approves, with gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putin's' marks the word as Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and statistics, often numerical, so figures in the sense of numbers fits.

clue.text: His boxing would stop blood being shed

definitions.text: His boxing would stop blood being shed

blocks.clueFragment: His boxing would stop blood being shed
blocks.note: surface reading: a fighter whose boxing is so clean that nobody bleeds
setter's reading: putting him in a box, his coffin, would stop the vampire spilling blood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' is the sport on the surface, but means sealing someone in a box; 'blood being shed' is the vampire's victims bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's count is the most famous vampire, who sleeps in a coffin and drinks the blood of victims.

clue.text: Thai in a broadcast from another country

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Thai person appears in a programme transmitted from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thai' already names a nationality, which makes the clue look like it wants one; the answer is another, from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Haitian means belonging to Haiti, a Caribbean nation, so it is one example of coming from a foreign land.

clue.text: Nureyev conceivably is this attractive

blocks.note: surface reading: the famous ballet dancer was a striking man
setter's reading: the dancer's name holds the organ of sight in its middle letters

explanation.surface: The Russian ballet star Rudolf Nureyev was a dazzling sight.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: NUR-EYE-V is a name that catches an EYE, so 'conceivably' says the answer describes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attractive draws the gaze and stands out, which is the sense of the compound adjective.
